questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Italian culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received several e-mails with information regarding my arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty difficult to find something affordable, which I didn't succeed with, so my housing was pretty expensive during my exchange.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start looking as early as possible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: During the first week you have the opportunity to try out different courses. Then you register to the courses you want to follow at the website of the university. The most important thing was to register for the exams, but that was also pretty straight forward from my experience.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Mobility office at the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. There are no limitations in how many that can join each course, so all the courses I wanted to take were available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: From my experience, it is mostly the pre-approval process that can take a bit of time, however it all worked out, so try not to stress about it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of the courses were at the level that I am used to from back home, and some of the courses were at a lower level. None of the courses I took were more demanding than what I am used to from back home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More in-class discussions and more presentations by the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Geopolitics of Migrations
Globalization, Social Justice and Human Rights
Political Order, Violence and Institutions
Programming for Social Data Science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Political Order, Violence and Institutions, because the course was really well-structured. Furthermore, I would recommend Programming for Social Data Science, if you are interested in being introduced to machine learning methods.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Since I had to do my exams by hand, I had to buy pencils, pencil sharpener etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing ended up being more expensive than what I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a cultural club that arranged different cultural activities such as going to the theatre. Furthermore, there was a social network for Erasmus students that arranged social events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't join any non-academic activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Beside exploring Milano, I would recommend visiting other Italian cities, because they are easy to reach by train, and the train tickets were pretty affordable.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: After the first week, it was relatively easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to talk to people in class or join one of the non-academic clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were no cultural differences that were particularly challenging from my experience.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cultural sights, the food culture and the fact that the weather allows you to be outside most of the time, which I really appreciated.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Start to look for housing as early as possible. 2. It can sometimes be a bit challenging going on exchange, however it was all worth it from my experience. 3. Try not to stress too much about the pre-approval process. From my experience, it all worked out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I took all my exams during December, which was a bit stressful, however it was manageable from my experience. If you have the opportunity, maybe take some of the exams both in December and January.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of international students in Milano, and it was really rewarding for me to be in an international environment and study with people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge for me was all the administrative work that had to be done in preparing for the exchange. I also found the exam period a bit challenging. I find exams stressful back home too, so doing exams in a foreign environment was bit challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
